terms.gloss: serve up, set food before someone
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 2.4.69: adposita sit cēna (Lewis & Short)
Lewis & Short s.v. appōnō: of food, to serve up
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “freq. as t. t. of food, dishes, to serve up, set before one”. Ministrāre is to wait on the person; appōnere is to put the dish on the table.

terms.gloss: be a slave to (not “serve at table”)
terms.comment: Traupman gives servīre for serving a person at table (Possumne tibi nunc servīre?); classically it means to be a slave or to be devoted to someone (Lewis & Short). A waiter ministrat.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 67; pp. 68, 73.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 164, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.

phrases.english: I’ll serve your meal as soon as I can.
